firms.notes: Hedge fund; acquired McClatchy out of bankruptcy in 2020. Also controls Canada's Postmedia and American Media (publisher of the National Enquirer).
Managed GateHouse Media / New Media Investment Group, which merged with Gannett in 2019 to form the largest US newspaper chain. (Fortress itself has been owned by SoftBank and later Mubadala.)

businesses.platform_company: Alden's flagship newspaper group (formerly Digital First Media), Denver Post, San Jose Mercury News, St. Paul Pioneer Press, Boston Herald and dozens more; Alden controls 200+ US papers

evidence.description: After taking over MediaNews Group out of bankruptcy in 2010, Alden cut newsroom staffing by more than 75% across its papers, and its 2016 consolidation of eight San Francisco Bay Area papers into two triggered mass layoffs. Alden's playbook, gutting newsrooms and selling off real estate, was the subject of The Atlantic's 2021 cover story 'The Men Who Are Killing America's Newspapers.'

businesses.platform_company: Chicago Tribune, New York Daily News, Orlando Sentinel, Hartford Courant and more (Baltimore Sun later sold); Alden bought Tribune Publishing for $633M in 2021

evidence.description: After Alden's $633M takeover of Tribune Publishing in 2021, papers such as the Chicago Tribune quickly lost about a quarter of their newsroom to buyouts, thinning coverage of state and local government. Sens. Dick Durbin and Tammy Duckworth publicly pressed Alden over the 'alarming' staff cuts.

businesses.platform_company: 2nd-largest US newspaper chain, 30 papers including the Miami Herald, Sacramento Bee, Kansas City Star and Charlotte Observer

evidence.description: McClatchy carried heavy debt from its $4.5B 2006 purchase of Knight-Ridder and filed for Chapter 11 in Feb 2020. Hedge fund Chatham Asset Management, its longtime lead lender, won the bankruptcy auction in July 2020, ending 163 years of family control and handing the chain to its creditors.

businesses.platform_company: Largest US newspaper company, 260+ dailies including USA Today; assembled via the 2019 GateHouse–Gannett merger. Now publicly traded (NYSE: GCI) after internalizing management ~2020

evidence.description: Fortress-managed New Media Investment Group (owner of GateHouse) merged with Gannett in 2019 to form the largest US newspaper chain, a ~$1.4B deal funded partly by a ~$1.79B loan from Apollo Global at ~11.5% interest. GateHouse cut roughly 200 staff in the first half of 2019, and cost-cutting and layoffs continued across the merged papers.
